validation.release_build: cargo build --release succeeded in TRust; release engine and test runners also built

limits: The 60 FPS / 50–100x goal is not achieved.
Headless real-WebGL browser-controller measurements exclude native desktop-window presentation.
Three fresh processes per version, interleaved ABBAAB; bootstrap intervals are descriptive with only three process replicates.
Ordinary background applications remained running; benchmark processes used the CPU affinities in the manifests.
Kernel timings are isolated engine workloads and do not predict a scene-level speedup.
ARM64 native backend measured on NVIDIA GB10; x86-64 reviewed for shared-layout compatibility but not executed.
The full Test262 suite was not run. Budget-skipped differential programs are inconclusive.

provenance.method: Six sequential runs, three of each binary in ABBAAB order. Both have identical TRust/WebGL sources; only the TRust JS engine differs. Completed rAF tasks beginning at or after 25s. Callback time excludes task checkpoint, presentation, and scheduling; start-to-start intervals include them. Headless controller uses real WebGL, excludes native desktop window presentation.

diagnosis: The measured page uses native ARM64 JIT code and NVIDIA EGL/GLES. CPU profiles show repeated TRust JS runtime calls; they do not show software rasterization as the cause of the remaining gap.
Numeric array templates did not cover both current packed element representations. A missing optional numeric mirror could replay the rest of an arithmetic chain through generic opcode helpers.
Numeric loop conditions using strict inequality could enter a helper sequence on every iteration. Same-type Number comparisons now stay native, preserving NaN and signed-zero semantics.

Computed reads discarded per-operation scratch IC state and repeatedly resolved/copied property keys. Ordinary for-in loops repeatedly rebuilt the same key lists. The changes reuse bounded, guarded caches.
Negative property caches were too shallow for common class prototype chains; missing flags caused repeated complete property searches.
TypedArray.set from an ordinary numeric Array performed generic indexed reads and temporary byte-vector allocation per element. A guarded whole-source proof allows direct ordered copying.

The remaining architectural limitation is a template JIT with many operation-level guards and owned Value/runtime-helper boundaries. These measurements do not establish one remaining switch or bug capable of a 50–100x improvement.

profiling_evidence.method: Local ARM64 ptrace stack samples (1400 samples after startup) and opt-in JIT helper counters. Symbol builds are diagnostic, separate from final release timings.
profiling_evidence.interpretation: Inclusive percentages overlap and include descendants. run_vm does not mean interpreter self time, and jit_direct_finish includes tail-call work. Driver CPU samples are not GPU utilization or GPU execution time.
profiling_evidence.helper_example: An intermediate profile recorded 1,287,460 calls each at the LoadLocal/StrictNotEq/GetElemLocal sequence in arraysEqual; this motivated native comparison and packed-array support.
profiling_evidence.native_call_architecture: The strict recursive numerical fixture emits 1412 ARM64 instruction words (5648 bytes) in both the baseline and final candidate, including guards, fallbacks and shared call stubs. Direct calls still check recursion/GC, obtain a frame, move owned Values, save/swap JitCtx fields and finish through runtime cleanup. This is evidence of a heavyweight calling convention; generated code size alone is not executed instruction count or time.

standards.freshness: Official local snapshot; not asserted to be verified current upstream text.

architecture_reference.note: Mozilla documents the distinction between baseline template compilation and the optimizing Warp/Ion pipeline. Firefox 60+ FPS is user-reported; no controlled Firefox run was performed here.

correctness_fixes: A pre-existing mirror store clobbered the Number register while checking whether it was an integer, losing fractions and negative zero.
NaN payloads are canonicalized when stored into NaN-boxed property words, preserving Number classification.

Commit f37febe fixes 16 pre-existing Test262 failures: absent TypedArray indices after resizing/detachment must remain absent for HasProperty-based Array iteration/search methods. Baseline failures were reproduced independently.
promotion: Source commits and local release artifacts only. Installed binaries were not overwritten and commits were not pushed.
memory_interpretation: The standalone kernel peak RSS medians increase by about 2.57 MiB. In separate smaps observations the total increase is 2448 KiB, of which 2388 KiB is file-backed executable residency and 60 KiB is heap/anonymous storage. Post-GC managed requested bytes increase by 81,873 bytes (a lower-bound accounting difference). The new enumeration cache is bounded to 256 entries and a 1 MiB payload budget. Scene peak RSS medians differ by under 1%, within the observed run variation. This is a bounded cache/code-residency tradeoff, recorded separately from throughput; no claim of reduced memory use is made.

warmup_sensitivity.note: Recomputed from the same six runs; not additional independent trials.

resource_diagnostics.note: Separate diagnostic runs with TRUST_JS_PERF_METRICS=1; not mixed into normal timing distributions. Managed memory is a post-GC lower bound where labeled.
